pr_title: [Hardware][Apple] Native support for macOS Apple Silicon
pr_body:
Add some adjustments on ARM/CPU build scripts to build and run directly on Mac Os with Apple Chip.

Summary:

- Added some conditional setup on build to consider Mac Os as a valid device
- Adjusted some intrinsics implementation to proper work with Clang
- Set NUMA as optional for build on CPU and automatically disabled on Apple Silicon Build.  
- Minor docs update.

In general, the build instruction to build on Mac Os is identical to CPU build `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pip install -e .`, the changes on this PR should make sure it works.

**EDIT:**

Added a small workaround to fix the following error when running the API server:

```
ERROR:    [Errno 48] error while attempting to bind on address ('0.0.0.0', 8000): address already in use
````

I saw in past code that something similar was being done. To keep the current implementation, only when the OS is macOS, it will reuse the bound socket on the server startup. 

FIX #10658 (*link existing issues this PR will resolve*)

---
Comment: I tried my best to not change too much the base code. I hope more people try and send feedback and will be happy to make adjustment and improvements.

review_comments:
I'm curious what led to making this change and why it's darwin specific?

We previously set `fd=sock.fileno()` in all cases here, but I removed it because of some odd unexpected behavior that turned out to be because this option is not doing what we expected. I don't think this is right, but I'd like to propose an alternative for whatever issue was encountered.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10012

I think I found it ... you left this comment prior to making the change:

> Hey @mgoin did you have a chance to actually try on a mac os with Apple Chip? Before open this PR I tested only the offline inference, which is working very well so far. But I am having issues with the server. I am having this error:
> 
> ERROR:    [Errno 48] error while attempting to bind on address ('0.0.0.0', 8000): address already in use
I tried to change the port, and inspect if the port is actually being used, but no luck. If you tested, can you please give me a feedback with that? I'd like to know if this is an issue of my machine. Thank you!

If that's the error, I think I know the right fix. I'll post a link to a PR here after I post something.

Yes, you got it. 

> One side-effect of this change is that uvicorn no longer emits a
message showing the host and port number in use when it starts the
server, so this includes a new INFO log message on the vLLM side that
does the same thing prior to starting the server.

I found that solution too, but the lack of the message with feedback made me give up of this. Also I avoided to change behavior on other platforms, that is why I did the change only to make it work on macOS.
